note: First draft from v2 section 7 for Laurence to read and edit before any real score. A change is a new version. Ten tests a dimension, each yes or no with a one line evidence.

tests.question: Does the idea answer the brief's single-minded proposition?
tests.pass_when: The idea is plainly a way of saying the proposition, and nothing else is competing with it.

tests.question: Could a competitor not run this idea with their name on it?
tests.pass_when: Swapping the brand name for a rival's makes the idea stop working.

tests.question: Is the idea absent from the agency's Banned list?
tests.pass_when: No Banned-list match is recorded on the work.

tests.question: Could a journalist headline it in one line?
tests.pass_when: A single sentence says what the idea is without the brand name explaining it.

tests.question: Is it one thought?
tests.pass_when: The idea can be said once and the second half does not argue with the first.

tests.question: Does it start from the brief's insight?
tests.pass_when: The idea visibly grows out of the insight and does not ignore it.

tests.question: Would the audience repeat it to a friend?
tests.pass_when: It is easy to retell, and a friend would get it without the ad.

tests.question: Does it say something the audience does not expect from this category?
tests.pass_when: It breaks a category habit and does not repeat one.

tests.question: Is it said in 30 words or fewer?
tests.pass_when: The work's idea line is 30 words or fewer.

tests.question: Does it give the audience a reason to believe it?
tests.pass_when: The idea carries, or points at, one of the brief's reasons to believe.

tests.question: Is it tied to the brief's objective?
tests.pass_when: The work would move the objective the brief names and nothing else.

tests.question: Can its effect be measured with the brief's measure?
tests.pass_when: One of the brief's measures would show whether it worked.

tests.question: Does it say what people will feel or do?
tests.pass_when: A person can say what the audience will feel or do after meeting it.

tests.question: Does it deal with the barrier the brief names?
tests.pass_when: The work takes on the barrier and does not step round it.

tests.question: Does it answer the audience's objection?
tests.pass_when: The objection is met in the work, not left for the audience to resolve.

tests.question: Does it do the job the brief gives the work?
tests.pass_when: It does what the brief's job line asks of this piece of work.

tests.question: Is it made for the audience the brief names?
tests.pass_when: The language and the world belong to that audience.

tests.question: Does it keep the brief's tone?
tests.pass_when: The tone is the tone the brief sets, not a neighbour of it.

tests.question: Is it free of anything the brief rules out?
tests.pass_when: Nothing in the work breaks a mandatory or a limit the brief sets.

tests.question: Is the next step for the audience clear?
tests.pass_when: A person can see what to do or think next.

tests.question: Is every mandatory line in the script?
tests.pass_when: Each mandatory line the checks list appears in the beats.

tests.question: Is every banned word absent?
tests.pass_when: No banned word from the checks appears in the beats.

tests.question: Does it fit the slot?
tests.pass_when: For a timed format the words read within the slot at 2.5 words a second, with a second to spare.

tests.question: Is it free of em and en dashes?
tests.pass_when: No beat holds an em or an en dash.

tests.question: Is there at least one line to say?
tests.pass_when: At least one beat has words in it.

tests.question: Does the first line earn the second?
tests.pass_when: The opening line gives the listener a reason to stay.

tests.question: Does each beat add something new?
tests.pass_when: No beat only repeats the one before it.

tests.question: Does it sound like a person saying it?
tests.pass_when: Read aloud it is speech, not copy.

tests.question: Does it end on the brand line or the proposition?
tests.pass_when: The last beat lands the idea.

tests.question: Does every word earn its place?
tests.pass_when: Cutting any beat would lose something that matters.

tests.question: Does the route state its bet?
tests.pass_when: The route has a bet of one sentence.

tests.question: Does it hold at least one card?
tests.pass_when: At least one card is in the route.

tests.question: Did the team write the cards first?
tests.pass_when: Every card in the route was first written by a person.

tests.question: Is the route named?
tests.pass_when: The route has a name of one to six words.

tests.question: Is the bet short?
tests.pass_when: The bet is 35 words or fewer.

tests.question: Could the bet be proved wrong?
tests.pass_when: A result could show the bet was wrong.

tests.question: Do the cards point the same way?
tests.pass_when: The cards are parts of one route and do not pull apart.

tests.question: Could the team make it with the means the brief gives?
tests.pass_when: Budget, time and channels in the brief allow it.

tests.question: Is it clear what to make first?
tests.pass_when: A first piece of work follows plainly from the route.

tests.question: Does it stretch into more than one piece of work?
tests.pass_when: The route can make more than one thing and stay itself.

tests.question: Does it name a territory with its line?
tests.pass_when: The territory has a name and a one sentence line.

tests.question: Does it say what must show?
tests.pass_when: At least one must-show line is written.

tests.question: Does it say what must never show?
tests.pass_when: At least one never-show line is written.

tests.question: Does it carry the tone?
tests.pass_when: At least one tone word is written.

tests.question: Does it carry a reference frame?
tests.pass_when: At least one reference frame is attached.

tests.question: Is the territory clear enough to shoot from?
tests.pass_when: A person could picture the first frame from the line.

tests.question: Do the must-show and never-show lines agree?
tests.pass_when: No line contradicts another.

tests.question: Can the proposition be seen in it?
tests.pass_when: The proposition would show in the pictures.

tests.question: Is the product's place in the picture clear?
tests.pass_when: It says how the product shows.

tests.question: Is it unlike what the category already looks like?
tests.pass_when: The look is not the category's usual look.
